title: The Vineyard Song
summary: The narrator announces a song concerning his beloved’s vineyard on a fruitful hill. The song recounts fencing, stone removal, planting the choicest vine, and construction of a tower and wine-press. Expected grapes give way to wild grapes.
characters: Nephi (narrator; identified by the task, not explicitly named in these verses)
locations: The song’s vineyard on a very fruitful hill; the narrator’s location is unspecified

explicit_facts.text: The first-person narrator announces that he will sing a song concerning his beloved’s vineyard.
The song describes the well-beloved as having a vineyard on a very fruitful hill.
The song recounts that he fenced the vineyard, removed its stones, planted the choicest vine, built a tower in its midst, and made a wine-press.
He expected grapes, but the vineyard brought forth wild grapes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A clearly illustrative, static image of the song’s vineyard may include the fence, vine, tower, wine-press, and wild grapes, without reenacting its preparation or implying a witnessed event.
unspecified_visual_details: The narrator’s physical appearance and setting.
The well-beloved’s identity and appearance.
The vineyard’s layout, architectural forms, colors, and the appearance of its wild grapes.

narration.text: And then will I sing to my well-beloved a song of my beloved, touching his vineyard.
My well-beloved hath a vineyard in a very fruitful hill.
and he looked that it should bring forth grapes, and it brought forth wild grapes.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Attribute the narration to Nephi according to the task’s explicit identification; these two verses do not independently name the first-person narrator.
The vineyard belongs to the song’s content, not a separately narrated witnessed scene.
These verses do not explain what the vineyard or well-beloved represents.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a physical appearance or divine identity for the well-beloved.
Do not stage the vineyard’s preparation and fruit production as simultaneous present action.
Do not invent a singing audience, narrator location, or visible divine appearance.
Do not claim that these verses explicitly name Nephi.

title: Judge the Vineyard
summary: The speaker asks Jerusalem's inhabitants and Judah's men to judge between him and his vineyard, asking what more could have been done.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker addresses Jerusalem's inhabitants and Judah's men and asks them to judge between him and his vineyard.
The speaker asks what more could have been done, noting that the vineyard produced wild grapes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The vineyard may be shown as the setting for the speech.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
Whether any addressees are visibly present.

narration.text: judge, I pray you, betwixt me and my vineyard.
What could have been done more to my vineyard

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is an appeal framed through the vineyard figure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Jerusalem's inhabitants or Judah's men listening; their visible presence is not stated.

title: The Vineyard Laid Waste
summary: The speaker declares that the vineyard's hedge and wall will be removed, and that it will be left waste, unworked, and without rain.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says the hedge will be removed, the vineyard eaten up, and its wall broken down and trodden down.
The speaker says the vineyard will be laid waste, unpruned and undug, with briers and thorns; he will command the clouds not to rain upon it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The vineyard may appear neglected, with broken boundaries and briers.
unspecified_visual_details: Whether the threatened destruction is shown as happening now or only described.
Clouds, weather, and the vineyard's exact condition.

narration.text: I will take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be eaten up;
I will lay it waste; it shall not be pruned nor digged;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vineyard is a figure, not a separately narrated literal event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not present the threatened future actions as events that have already occurred.

title: The Vineyard Identified
summary: The vineyard is identified as the house of Israel, and Judah as the pleasant plant; the Lord looked for judgment and righteousness but found oppression and a cry.

explicit_facts.text: The vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah are his pleasant plant.
He looked for judgment and found oppression, and for righteousness but found a cry.

unspecified_visual_details: Any visible people or location.

narration.text: the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel,

for righteousness, but behold, a cry.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The vineyard language is explicitly interpreted in this verse.
prohibited_inventions: Do not turn the metaphor into a literal scene of people transformed into plants.

title: House upon House
summary: A woe is pronounced against those who join house to house for solitary possession; desolation of houses and cities and poor agricultural yield are declared.

explicit_facts.text: A woe is pronounced against those who join house to house until they are alone in the midst of the earth.
The Lord of Hosts says many houses shall be desolate and great, fair cities without inhabitants.
Ten acres of vineyard shall yield one bath, and a homer of seed an ephah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A visual contrast between joined houses, empty dwellings, and scant vineyard yield.
unspecified_visual_details: Which houses or cities are meant, and their architecture.
Whether people are visible.

narration.text: Wo unto them that join house to house,

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The desolation is spoken of as a future consequence.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a named city or identify particular owners.

title: Feasting Without Regard
summary: A woe is pronounced against those who pursue strong drink from morning until night; their feasts include music and wine, while they disregard the Lord's work.

explicit_facts.text: Some rise early to follow strong drink and continue until night, with wine inflaming them.
Their feasts include harp, viol, tabret, pipe, and wine; they do not regard the work of the Lord or consider his hands' operation.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A feast with musical instruments and wine.
unspecified_visual_details: The attendees' identities, number, dress, and appearance.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The warning condemns excess and disregard for the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Do not assign names or biographies to feast attendees.

title: Captivity and Thirst
summary: The people go into captivity for lack of knowledge; their honored men famish, the multitude thirsts, and the people's glory and multitude descend into hell.

explicit_facts.text: The people are gone into captivity because they have no knowledge; their honorable men are famished and their multitude dried up with thirst.
Hell enlarges herself and opens her mouth without measure; the people's glory, multitude, pomp, and rejoicing one descend into it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Captivity and thirst may be conveyed without specifying a particular captor or location.
unspecified_visual_details: The captors, location, and appearance of captives.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The enlarged mouth of hell is figurative language; it is not a narrated visible being.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict hell as a literal creature or infer a supernatural visible event.

The Lord of Hosts is exalted in judgment, and God that is holy is sanctified in righteousness.

explicit_facts.text: As fire devours stubble and flame consumes chaff, their root shall be rottenness and blossoms shall go up as dust.

title: The Hills Tremble
summary: The Lord's anger is kindled; he stretches forth his hand, smites the people, the hills tremble, and carcasses lie torn in the streets; his anger is not turned away.
